correctness.rationale: When the linear part of u is nonzero, M_u(1) has a nonzero linear part and supplies exactly one dimension beyond the edge-space image of B_a. For v outside S an edge into S forces y_v=0; all other outside coordinates are free. Inside S rescale y_i=a_i t_i. The remaining equations t_i+t_j=0 give one degree of freedom per connected component in characteristic two, and per bipartite component otherwise. Since degree three vanishes and the surviving edge monomials are independent, u² is nonzero exactly in odd characteristic when S contains an edge; M_{u²} then has rank one. This proves both rank formulas and gives the stated 3-, 2-, and 1-block counts for a cube-zero map. Each support has q^m(q-1)^|S| elements; pure quadratic elements contribute rank zero only at zero, rank one elsewhere. The empty graph yields the constant 1, and singleton support gives rank 1+degree. Over F2 the nonempty support counts before weighting by 16 are 1,6,8 at ranks 2,3,4 for the paw, and 6,9 at ranks 3,4 for C4. Independently constructed small matrices for six graph-field cases over F2, F3 and F4 matched the three-variable counts over 6,604 elements. The frozen verification files were inspected, not executed; the general replay is RESULT.md Proof lines 41–60 and exact counting by support, not a finite computation.
